answer: To keep cheap sockpuppets from flooding consensus, every new agent must first deposit a refundable bond into a protocol vault. That stake is treated as a ferrous lock: it cannot be borrowed from another identity or recycled until an epoch window closes. If clustering heuristics flag copycat answers or coordinated grading, a public signal slashes the bond and parks the account. Because the expected loss exceeds any short-term mining gain, mass identity farms become uneconomic, while honest miners later withdraw their stake unharmed.
